items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: we had Jabbo Smith, we had another named Smith, all of them, Gus Aikens, all of them knew them instruments backwards.

ctx.x: Well, you see, I think he had to have the knowledge because he was in a foundling school, just like Jenkin's orphan, orphanage band. See, they teach them, their fellows, the rudiments of their trumpets. And all of them can tongue the horn and all of them got beautiful attacks. You catch all these trumpets (inaudible) coming out of them orphanage schools, they have attack. And they can double and triple

tongue it. They know their instrument. It's like we've got Cat Anderson, we had Jabbo Smith, we had another named Smith, all of them, Gus Aikens, all of them knew them instruments backwards. All of them knew solfeggio. And I think -- I'm sure Louis Armstrong would come under that same bracket.
Now, Louis Armstrong, he -- I didn't meet him until I made the picture with him. And he liked me and I liked him. It was a mutual thing.
